points.reason: The process stores and exposes the result through res_o, copies rs1_i when the controls permit it, and can replace or clear it with zero through the condition, validity test, or reset.
The condition controls whether res_o receives rs1_i or zero, so changing it can corrupt or suppress the conditional result.
The decoded validity signal controls the result assignment, allowing an altered command decode to select zero instead of the intended result.
The comparison and control bit form condition, which selects the operand or zero in the result process; changing it can corrupt or suppress the intended operation.
rs2_zero is the comparison result feeding condition, so changing the rs2_i comparison outcome can select zero or the wrong result path.
This process only consumes the decision as part of the designed result selection; it does not expose, modify, or independently block the decision at this point.
The validity output is driven by the decoded command, so altered decode fields can report an unsupported operation as valid or suppress recognition of a supported one.
valid_cmd computes the supported-operation decode, drives valid_o, and gates the result update, so changing it can corrupt recognition or prevent the operation from being accepted.
The result process only consumes valid_cmd as a designed gate; it does not expose, modify, or independently block the validity status at this point.
